sourcedFrom: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet (UNKNOWN — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: A sealed can, so this is maintenance, not a teardown. The RESONATOR R2 body is welded shut and nothing inside it comes out; what YHM publishes is how to get the can off the Phantom Q.D. mount, how to look after the outside, and — rarely — how to flush the inside with solvent without ever opening it. The two threaded joints that do open are the Phantom Q.D. adapter into the back of the body and the muzzle device onto the barrel, and both are in Deep Clean with their own torque figures. Note this booklet teaches the CAN. It contains no procedure for your firearm at all.

steps.title: Firearm unloaded and pointed somewhere safe before the can is touched
steps.action: Clear the host first and keep the muzzle in a safe direction for the whole job. YHM puts this at the top of its installation and removal section rather than assuming it, and the can coming on or off is exactly when a muzzle gets swung around a room.
steps.quote: BE CERTAIN THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND THE MUZZLE IS POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION BEFORE STARTING THIS REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION PROCESS.
steps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — INSTALLATION AND USE, PDF p.5 (the booklet prints no folio on any page)
steps.warn: Suppressed does not mean safe. YHM's own caution is that a suppressed firearm is just as dangerous as an unsuppressed one.

steps.title: This book covers the can, not your firearm
steps.action: Nothing in these twelve pages tells you how to unload, strip or service the host. YHM routes the firearm work to a gunsmith who knows your specific model, and the clearing procedure for your gun lives in your gun's own manual. Read this one for the suppressor and that one for the rifle.
steps.prose: That is a real bound on what is published here, not a disclaimer. There is no host-firearm procedure anywhere in the document.
steps.caution: Installing it wrong voids the warranty and, in YHM's words, removes any liabilities against the manufacturer.
steps.quote: ONLY A LICENSED GUNSMITH EXPERIENCED WITH YOUR MODEL OF FIREARM SHOULD INSTALL THIS PRODUCT.
steps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — INSTALLATION AND USE, PDF p.5

steps.title: Let it cool, then unscrew the can off the Q.D. mount
steps.action: Wait until the suppressor is cool enough to hold, then simply unscrew the body anticlockwise off the Phantom Q.D. mount. No tools are needed and none should be used — the whole point of the Q.D. system is that it goes on and comes off by hand.
steps.prose: Heat is the reason to wait. A thirty-round magazine of automatic fire puts the body 225°F above ambient, and it stays hot long after the last shot.
steps.quote: TO REMOVE THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR SIMPLY UNSCREW FROM THE Q.D. MOUNT.
steps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — SUPPRESSOR, PDF p.7
steps.warn: THE SUPPRESSOR CAN CAUSE SEVERE BURNS AND IGNITE FLAMMABLE MATERIALS.

steps.title: Check the mount is still tight — every time, not once
steps.action: With the can off, check that the Phantom Q.D. mount is still firmly on the barrel and that the adapter is still tight in the back of the suppressor. YHM asks for this periodically because firing walks these joints loose, and a loose can is a misaligned can.
steps.prose: This is the first item on YHM's own list of what causes baffle strikes, ahead of bad threads and bad ammunition.
steps.caution: IT IS IMPORTANT THAT THE USER PERIODICALLY CHECK TO ENSURE THAT THE SUPPRESSOR REMAINS FIRMLY ATTACHED TO THE FIREARM AND THE PHANTOM® Q.D. ADAPTER
steps.quote: IT IS POSSIBLE THAT WITH FIRING THE SUPPRESSOR MAY BECOME LOOSE, WHICH CAN CAUSE MISALIGNMENT.
steps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — NOTE, PDF p.3

steps.title: Wipe the outside down with a damp cloth
steps.action: Wipe oil, dirt and fouling off the outside of the tube with a damp cloth. That is the whole of the routine external service YHM publishes for this can — no solvent bath, no brushing, no abrasives on the cerakote.
steps.quote: EXCESS OIL, DIRT, AND OTHER CONTAMINANTS SHOULD BE WIPED FROM THE OUTSIDE SURFACE USING A DAMP CLOTH.
steps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8

steps.title: Take the can off the rifle when you are done shooting
steps.action: Do not leave it mounted in storage. Condensation trapped inside a suppressor is the single most common problem YHM sees, and pulling the can lets the moisture evaporate. If it has to stay on the rifle, store the rifle muzzle-down with the bolt open so the inside can drain and breathe.
steps.prose: Corrosion here is not cosmetic — it is happening on baffles you can never get to.
steps.aside: IF THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR IS TO REMAIN ON THE RIFLE, IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE RIFLE BE STORED IN A MUZZLE-DOWN POSITION WITH THE BOLT LEFT OPEN.
steps.quote: THE MOST COMMON PROBLEM ENCOUNTERED WHEN USING A SOUND SUPPRESSOR IS CORROSION CAUSED BY CONDENSATION BUILDUP INSIDE THE SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8

steps.title: Nothing wet or loose goes inside the tube
steps.action: Never fire the can with water, gel, grease or any other medium inside it. This is not about cleanliness — a suppressor with something in it is a pressure vessel with the volume filled, and YHM's stated consequence is damage to the can, damage to the host, or serious injury.
steps.prose: It also voids the warranty outright.
steps.quote: DO NOT USE THIS SOUND SUPPRESSOR WITH WATER OR ANY OTHER MEDIA INSIDE THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — WARNING!, PDF p.3
steps.warn: If you have soaked the can, it must be fully drained and blown dry before it goes back on a rifle.

steps.title: That is the whole field strip — the body does not open
steps.action: Can off the mount, mount checked, outside wiped. There is no further disassembly of the RESONATOR R2 published anywhere in the booklet: no baffle stack, no end cap, no core. Deep Clean covers the two joints that do come apart — the Phantom Q.D. adapter and the muzzle device — plus the solvent flush and the cleaning interval.
steps.prose: The published interval for the inside is 2000 to 3000 rounds, and YHM says the internals rarely need doing at all.
steps.quote: AS A GENERAL RULE, WE RECOMMEND CLEANING THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR AFTER EVERY 2000 TO 3000 ROUNDS.
steps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Phantom Q.D. adapter out of the back of the body
deepSteps.action: The adapter threads into the rear of the suppressor and is the only part of the can that comes off it. Grip the R2 body firmly, put the supplied wrench on the notches in the base of the adapter and back it out anticlockwise. Going back in it is hand-started to avoid cross-threading, then torqued to about 35 ft-lbs — clockwise, with the wrench on those same notches.
deepSteps.prose: Start the thread by hand every time. This is a proprietary mount and the adapter is not a part you want to gall.
deepSteps.aside: THREAD THE PHANTOM® Q.D. ADAPTER (1B) ASSEMBLY INTO THE RESONATOR® R2 SUPPRESSOR BODY (2B) BY HAND, TAKING CARE NOT TO CROSS-THREAD.
deepSteps.quote: HOLD THE RESONATOR® R2 BODY (2B) WITH A FIRM GRIP. USING THE SUPPLIED WRENCH (3B) TO GRASP THE NOTCHES IN THE BASE OF THE ADAPTER (1B), TIGHTEN THE ADAPTER IN A CLOCKWISE DIRECTION. TORQUE TO APPROXIMATELY 35 FT-LBS.
deepSteps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — PHANTOM® Q.D. ADAPTER, PDF p.5
deepSteps.warn: Adapter into the body: 35 ft-lbs. This is NOT the muzzle-device figure — see the next step.

deepSteps.title: Muzzle device on the barrel — 20-30 ft-lbs against a square shoulder
deepSteps.action: The Phantom Q.D. mount is proprietary and needs YHM's own matching muzzle device on the barrel. Fit it with a 3/4" open-end wrench and torque to 20-30 ft-lbs, and make sure it lands flat against a 90° barrel shoulder. If the mount needs clocking, use the shim kit that came with it.
deepSteps.prose: Two different joints, two different numbers: 35 ft-lbs for the adapter into the can, 20-30 ft-lbs for the device onto the barrel. Do not carry one onto the other.
deepSteps.aside: THE PHANTOM® Q.D. ADAPTER IS A PROPRIETARY MOUNTING SYSTEM, AND AS SUCH REQUIRES A COMPLEMENTARY MUZZLE DEVICE (INCLUDED).
deepSteps.quote: IT IS ESSENTIAL THAT THE MUZZLE DEVICE SEATS AGAINST A 90° BARREL SHOULDER.
deepSteps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — MUZZLE DEVICE, PDF p.6

deepSteps.title: The crush washer goes in the bin, and is never replaced with another
deepSteps.action: Strip off whatever muzzle device is on the barrel now and throw away the crush washer with it. Do not fit a new crush or peel washer under a suppressor mount. YHM voids the warranty over this by name, because those washers do not compress evenly and what they leave behind is an off-axis mount.
deepSteps.prose: Indexing is done with the supplied shim kit instead. That is what it is in the box for.
deepSteps.quote: *CRUSH WASHERS WILL VOID THE WARRANTY AS THEY DO NOT CRUSH UNIFORMLY AND WILL CAUSE IMPROPER MOUNTING AND BAFFLE STRIKES.*
deepSteps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — MUZZLE DEVICE, PDF p.6
deepSteps.warn: A crush washer, a peel washer, or anything else that causes misalignment voids the warranty on both the can and the host.

deepSteps.title: Solvent flush — done through the can, never into it
deepSteps.action: The inside rarely needs anything. When it does, YHM's published method is to submerge the whole suppressor in a hydrocarbon-based gun cleaning solvent. There is no dismantling in this: the can goes in whole and comes out whole.
deepSteps.prose: Kroil, or one part transmission fluid to two parts mineral spirits, are the mixes YHM names.
deepSteps.quote: CLEANING OF THE INTERNALS IS RARELY NECESSARY BUT CAN BE ACCOMPLISHED BY SUBMERGING THE SUPPRESSOR IN A HYDROCARBON BASED GUN CLEANING SOLVENT (SUCH AS KROIL OR A MIXTURE OF 1 PART TRANSMISSION FLUID AND 2 PARTS MINERAL SPIRITS).
deepSteps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Drain it, then blow it dry
deepSteps.action: Let all the solvent run out, then blow the remainder out with high-pressure air before the can goes anywhere near a rifle. A suppressor still wet inside is the media-filled can the WARNING page rules out, and firing it that way is what raises pressures dangerously.
deepSteps.quote: ALLOW THE SOLVENT TO DRAIN OUT OF THE SUPPRESSOR AND BLOW OUT ANY REMAINING SOLVENT USING A HIGH PRESSURE AIR HOSE.
deepSteps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8
deepSteps.warn: Do not shortcut the drying. Trapped solvent is trapped media.

deepSteps.title: Back on the mount until the ratchet stops
deepSteps.action: Slide the back of the body over the Phantom Q.D. mount until it stops, then turn it clockwise by hand. You will hear the locking mechanism click as it goes. Keep turning until the ratcheting stops — that, not a torque figure, is how you know it has sealed.
deepSteps.prose: No tools. If it needs tools to seat, something on the taper or the threads is dirty.
deepSteps.aside: TIGHTEN THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR FIRMLY UNTIL THE RATCHETING STOPS TO ENSURE A CORRECT SEAL.
deepSteps.quote: INSTALL THE RESONATOR® R2 BODY (2D) BY SLIDING THE BACK END OVER THE YHM® PHANTOM® Q.D. MOUNT (1D) UNTIL IT STOPS, THEN TURN THE SUPPRESSOR (2D) CLOCKWISE TO HAND TIGHTEN.
deepSteps.cite: the RESONATOR® R2 SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2130 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — SUPPRESSOR, PDF p.7

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE OF THE TUBE
tasks: Wipe excess oil, dirt and other contaminants off the outside surface with a damp cloth
Let the can reach a temperature you can hold before touching it
Do not abrade the matte black high-temp cerakote finish

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Clean the Phantom Q.D. mount and the rear of the body where they engage
Check the adapter is still tight in the back of the can — 35 ft-lbs
Check the muzzle device is still tight on the barrel — 20-30 ft-lbs against a 90° shoulder
Never fit a crush washer or peel washer under the mount; use the supplied shim kit to index

cleaning.name: INTERIOR — 2000 TO 3000 ROUNDS
tasks: Rarely necessary; when it is, submerge the whole can in a hydrocarbon-based gun cleaning solvent
Drain fully, then blow out the remaining solvent with high-pressure air
Never fire the can with water or any other media inside it
Do not attempt to open the body — no interior disassembly is published for the R2

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Take the suppressor off as soon as you have finished shooting so condensation can evaporate
If it stays on, store the rifle muzzle-down with the bolt open

reassembly: Hand-start the Phantom Q.D. adapter into the rear of the R2 body, then torque it to approximately 35 ft-lbs with the supplied wrench on the notches in the adapter base.
Fit YHM's matching muzzle device to a clean barrel thread against a 90° shoulder, 20-30 ft-lbs with a 3/4" open-end wrench, using the shim kit — never a crush washer — to index it.
Slide the body onto the Q.D. mount until it stops, then turn clockwise by hand.
Keep tightening until the ratcheting stops; that is the correct seal.
Confirm the can is bone dry inside if it has been soaked, before it goes on the rifle.
fncheck: With the firearm confirmed unloaded, check the suppressor is firmly attached to both the firearm and the Phantom Q.D. adapter, and that the ratchet has stopped. Anything that moves, rattles or will not seat comes back off — YHM lists the suppressor coming loose from the host as the number one cause of baffle strikes, ahead of poor barrel threads, incorrect mount installation and poor ammunition. Re-check the same joints periodically during shooting, not just before it.
